Location: All 84 Ganges Ghats (Central focus on Dashashwamedh, Rajghat, and Assi Ghat)
Description: Celebrated 15 days after Diwali on full moon night, where all 84 ghats are illuminated with over a million oil lamps (diyas), accompanied by riverfront cultural performances and laser shows.

Location: Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Tilbhandeshwar Temple, and citywide temple processions
Description: The night of Lord Shiva featuring grand Shiva Baraat (marriage processions), night-long temple rituals, continuous chanting, and intense devotion across the city.
A daily morning spiritual and cultural celebration featuring Vedic chanting, sunrise Ganga Aarti, classical music performances, and mass yoga sessions.
A famous 6-night classical music and dance festival featuring legendary Indian classical artists performing as a seva (service) to Lord Hanuman.
A 5-day state cultural festival held leading up to Dev Deepawali, highlighting classical music, folk dance performances, local crafts, and traditional sports.
A unique Varanasi tradition where devotees play Holi with sacred pyre ashes (bhasma) and gulal at the cremation ghat, celebrating the playful spirit of Lord Shiva.

Location: All major Ganges Ghats (Assi Ghat, Dashashwamedh, Namo Ghat)
Description: A sacred 4-day festival dedicated to the Sun God (Surya Dev) where thousands of devotees offer prayers and holy water dips at riverfront steps during sunset and sunrise.

Location: Ramnagar Fort and various outdoor grounds in Ramnagar
Description: The world's oldest continuous open-air theater performance, lasting nearly a month with no electric lights or microphones, enacted under the patronage of the Kashi Royal Family.
A 3-night musical festival exclusively dedicated to the ancient Dhrupad genre of Indian classical music, attracting master vocalists and enthusiasts worldwide.

Location: Sarnath Archaeological Complex & Mulagandha Kuti Vihar
Description: Commemorating the birth, enlightenment, and parinirvana of Lord Buddha with international Buddhist processions, monk chanting, relic displays, and garden prayers.
A grand festival of food offerings where Goddess Annapurna is adorned with a solid gold idol (revealed once a year) and presented with 56 traditional food delicacies.
Marks the sun's transit into Capricorn; celebrated with holy dips in the Ganges, kite flying on ghat rooftops, and eating sesame sweets (til-gur) and khichdi.
A famous 400-year-old traditional reenactment of Lord Krishna jumping into the Ganges to subdue the multi-hooded serpent Kaliya, performed on a large wooden kadamba branch.

Location: 50-mile pilgrimage circuit around sacred Kashi boundary
Description: An ancient 5-day barefoot circumambulation around the sacred perimeter of Varanasi, visiting 108 shrines along the rural boundary path.
A month-long holy bathing tradition where pilgrims take pre-sunrise dips in the Ganges and float small floating clay lamps on leaves down the river every evening.
